That Codex process had already exited around 09:23, so the lineage was retargeted and the same TTY came up as `berobu` — stuck at status `blank`, subject `codex`. Its watcher could not bind the thread because `rolloutFromTitle` only accepted an exact title match or a `"<name> | <dir>"` suffix. Slab decorates the window title *around* the thread name:

```
aesthetic-computer — Monitor prox:zamofu | aesthetic-computer — codex ◂ codex-slab — 74×19
```

I made the matcher split the title on the separators Terminal and Slab insert (`—`, `◂`, `|`) and accept a whole segment equal to the thread name. #!/bin/bash
# slab-tracked Codex launcher.
#
# Registers this Codex session as a "prompt rock" so it shows up in the slab
# menubar + prox exactly like a Claude session. Codex fires no per-event hooks
# the way Claude Code does, so instead we:
#   1. write an active-prompts marker (agent_type=codex) up front,
#   2. run a background watcher that tails Codex's rollout JSONL and flips the
#      shared state files (active-prompts / awaiting-prompts / running-tools)
#      on task_started / task_complete — the same files the Claude hooks touch,
#      so the menubar's state→color reducer needs zero Codex-specific logic,
#   3. clean everything up when Codex exits (or gets reaped if the tab dies,
#      since the marker carries agent_pid).
#
# Invoked by the `co` / `cor` fish shortcuts. Run `codex` directly to skip
# tracking.
set -u
SLAB_HOME=${SLAB_HOME:-$HOME/.local/share/slab}
SLAB_BIN=${SLAB_BIN:-$HOME/.local/bin}
ACTIVE_DIR="$SLAB_HOME/state/active-prompts"
AWAITING_DIR="$SLAB_HOME/state/awaiting-prompts"
RUNNING_DIR="$SLAB_HOME/state/running-tools"
mkdir -p "$ACTIVE_DIR" "$AWAITING_DIR" "$RUNNING_DIR"

# No jq or codex? Fall back to a plain, untracked codex so the shortcut never
# breaks the user's ability to launch it.
if ! command -v codex >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "codex not found on PATH" >&2
    exit 127
fi
if ! command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    exec codex "$@"
fi

sid=$(uuidgen)
export SLAB_PROMPT_SESSION_ID="$sid"
begin=$(date +%s)
# The wrapper (this bash process) is the parent of codex and holds the tab's
# controlling tty — use it for liveness + terminal-close, matching claude_pid.
tty=${SLAB_TERMINAL_TTY:-$(ps -o tty= -p $$ 2>/dev/null | tr -d ' ')}
cwd=$PWD
ts=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)

# Codex probes its terminal colors once. Set Slab's page BEFORE launching it,
# then retain that appearance while its status hues change during the session.
terminal_dark=null
if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "$SLAB_BIN/slab-prepare-terminal.mjs" ]]; then
    terminal_dark=$(node "$SLAB_BIN/slab-prepare-terminal.mjs" "$tty" 2>/dev/null) || terminal_dark=null
fi
case "$terminal_dark" in true|false|null) ;; *) terminal_dark=null ;; esac

# Fresh window reads "blank" (like Claude's SessionStart) until the first turn.
jq -n \
    --arg sid "$sid" --arg cwd "$cwd" --arg tty "$tty" \
    --arg pid "$$" --arg ts "$ts" \
    --argjson terminal_dark "$terminal_dark" \
    --arg nudge "${SLAB_NUDGE_SCREEN:-}" --arg contact "${SLAB_LOOPBOY_CONTACT:-}" \
    --arg event "${SLAB_LOOPBOY_EVENT:-}" --arg source "${SLAB_LOOPBOY_SOURCE:-}" \
    '{session_id:$sid, cwd:$cwd, subject:"codex session", summary:"codex",
      tty:$tty, agent_pid:($pid|tonumber), agent_type:"codex",
      updated:$ts, state:"blank", terminal_dark:$terminal_dark, nudge_screen:$nudge, loopboy_contact:$contact, loopboy_event:$event, loopboy_source:$source}' \
    > "$ACTIVE_DIR/$sid" 2>/dev/null

# Background watcher: derives per-turn state from the rollout JSONL.
watcher=""
if command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f "$SLAB_BIN/codex-session-watch.mjs" ]]; then
    node "$SLAB_BIN/codex-session-watch.mjs" "$sid" "$begin" "$$" "$tty" "$cwd" \
        >/dev/null 2>&1 &
    watcher=$!
fi

cleanup() {
    [[ -n "$watcher" ]] && kill "$watcher" 2>/dev/null
    rm -f "$ACTIVE_DIR/$sid" "$AWAITING_DIR/$sid" "$RUNNING_DIR/$sid"
}
agent_pid=""
stop_agent() {
    trap - INT TERM
    if [[ -n "$agent_pid" ]] && kill -0 "$agent_pid" 2>/dev/null; then
        kill -TERM "$agent_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
        for _ in {1..10}; do
            kill -0 "$agent_pid" 2>/dev/null || break
            sleep 0.05
        done
        kill -KILL "$agent_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
        wait "$agent_pid" 2>/dev/null || true
    fi
    exit 143
}
trap cleanup EXIT
trap stop_agent INT TERM

# Loopboys are background client loops, never fleet/UI operators. Remove the
# browser surfaces at process startup; the proxy separately scopes its private
# inbox to the named contact and session identity.
codex_guard_args=()
if [[ -n "${SLAB_LOOPBOY_EVENT:-}" && -z "${SLAB_LOOPBOY_CONTACT:-}" ]]; then
    codex_guard_args+=(
        -c 'mcp_servers.prox={url="http://127.0.0.1:7773/mcp", env_http_headers={"x-slab-prompt-session-id"="SLAB_PROMPT_SESSION_ID"}}'
    )
fi
if [[ -n "${SLAB_LOOPBOY_CONTACT:-}" ]]; then
    codex_guard_args+=(
        -c 'mcp_servers.prox={url="http://127.0.0.1:7773/mcp", env_http_headers={"x-slab-loopboy-contact"="SLAB_LOOPBOY_CONTACT", "x-slab-prompt-session-id"="SLAB_PROMPT_SESSION_ID"}}'
        -c 'mcp_servers.puppet.enabled=false'
        -c 'mcp_servers.frame.enabled=false'
        -c 'mcp_servers.fleet.enabled=false'
        --disable browser_use
        --disable browser_use_external
        --disable browser_use_full_cdp_access
        --disable in_app_browser
    )
fi

# Keep Codex on this wrapper's foreground process group and explicitly attach
# its streams to the controlling TTY. Running it as a managed child lets a ZZZ
# SIGTERM reach the actual agent before the wrapper exits, without closing the
# terminal that will carry the resume receipt.
# macOS still ships Bash 3.2, where expanding an empty array under `set -u`
# raises "unbound variable". Keep the guarded and ordinary launch forms
# explicit so the everyday `co` path never touches an empty array expansion.
if (( ${#codex_guard_args[@]} )); then
    codex "${codex_guard_args[@]}" "$@" < "/dev/$tty" > "/dev/$tty" 2>&1 &
else
    codex "$@" < "/dev/$tty" > "/dev/$tty" 2>&1 &
fi
agent_pid=$!
# From this point on, lifecycle managers must signal the actual Codex process,
# not this Bash wrapper. Bash defers TERM traps while it waits for a child;
# tracking the wrapper here could therefore orphan Codex when ZZZ parks it.
marker_tmp="$ACTIVE_DIR/.$sid.$$.tmp"
if jq --arg pid "$agent_pid" --arg wrapper "$$" \
    '.agent_pid=($pid|tonumber) | .wrapper_pid=($wrapper|tonumber)' \
    "$ACTIVE_DIR/$sid" > "$marker_tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
    mv "$marker_tmp" "$ACTIVE_DIR/$sid"
else
    rm -f "$marker_tmp"
fi
wait "$agent_pid"
status=$?
agent_pid=""
exit "$status"
[exit 0]

`prox:ribefa` pointed at Codex session `BA801EC4`. That Codex process had already exited around 09:23, so the lineage was retargeted and the same TTY came up as `berobu` — stuck at status `blank`, subject `codex`. ```

With no binding, the rock never learned which rollout to tail, so it stayed blank forever. I made the matcher split the title on the separators Terminal and Slab insert (`—`, `◂`, `|`) and accept a whole segment equal to the thread name. A plain substring test would have been wrong — it would match `codex` inside `codex-slab` and across the `prox:zamofu` segment, so the equality-on-a-segment check keeps the existing "never guess between concurrent windows" guard intact. I also escaped the directory before it goes into a `RegExp`.
